name: After Effects Path And Counter Motion
use_when: A Reel needs to show progress, growth, process steps, experience gain, or a path through a system.
An icon should move along a drawn line or route.
A number should count up or down as part of a proof or progress visual.
avoid_when: The number or path is decorative and does not clarify the spoken point.
The viewer cannot understand what the counter represents.
The path motion would distract from the speaker or proof.

timeline_pattern.pattern: draw_path_at_final_size -> copy_shape_path -> paste_to_icon_position -> ease_path_keyframes -> add_trim_paths_to_line -> add_slider_counter -> sync_to_spoken_progress
timeline_pattern.path_rule: Draw the final path at the actual size before copying it into Position; resizing the path afterward can create wrong motion.
timeline_pattern.counter_rule: Use Slider Control linked to Source Text for animated numbers, then ease the slider speed for readability.
timeline_pattern.sync_rule: Path, counter, and spoken concept should reach their key points together.

motion.rule: Animate path drawing and object movement together so the route feels intentional.

keyframe_values.trim_path: Use End 0 to 100 for line drawing and ease the keyframes.
keyframe_values.counter_start: Start from 0 or a nearby value when a full 0-to-target count is too fast.
keyframe_values.counter_ease: Slow the counter near the final number so the value can be read.
keyframe_values.path_copy: Copy the shape path after final sizing/positioning, then paste it into the object's Position.

sound.rule: Small ticks or count sounds can support numbers only if they do not clutter speech.

captions.rule: Avoid placing captions over the path or final counter value.

color.rule: Path, icon, and counter colors should match the scene palette and remain readable over the background.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use pre-rendered path/counter animation from AE/Remotion for best quality; simple counters can be approximated with drawtext expressions.
implementation.remotion: Represent path as points, iconPosition as interpolated path progress, trimPathProgress, and counterValue interpolated with easing.
implementation.blender: Use curve paths with follow-path constraints and animated text values when 3D depth is needed.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use manual keyframes along a route and animated number templates if available, then preview for readability.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use After Effects for shape paths, Trim Paths, pasted path Position keyframes, Slider Control counters, and Source Text expressions.

common_mistakes: Copying a path before resizing it and getting unexpected icon movement.
Counting too fast for the viewer to read the final value.
Letting a route line draw after the icon has already arrived.
Using a counter without explaining what it measures.
Covering the counter with captions or other text.
qc: The path motion clarifies a process, growth, or relationship.
The icon follows the intended visible line.
The line draw and icon movement are synchronized.
The counter final value is readable before the scene changes.
Captions and other overlays do not cover the path or counter.
